P0001.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit/Open
P0001.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. P0001 is set when the control module detects that the control circuit of this valve is open, i.e. no plausible current flows when the valve is driven. Rail pressure can then no longer be controlled as intended. Whether the valve is open or closed without current depends on the design, so the same fault can cause excess pressure in one system and no pressure in another.

causes.label: Connector at the regulator loose, corroded or unplugged
Solenoid coil of the regulator open
Broken wire in the harness, e.g. chafing or rodent damage
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start, or stalls (normally closed valve)
Loss of power or limp mode (normally open valve)

P0002.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0002.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. With P0002 the circuit is electrically intact, but command and effect do not match: the measured current does not fit the duty cycle, or rail pressure does not follow the regulator position plausibly. The cause is often mechanical, for example a sticking valve, rather than the wiring.

causes.label: Regulator sticking or worn due to dirt, debris or water in the fuel
High resistance at connector or wiring causing wrong current
Low-pressure supply problem: clogged filter or air in the fuel
Rail pressure sensor reading wrong values

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P0003.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit Low
P0003.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. On some output stages an open circuit is also reported as low. A short on the switched ground side can keep the valve permanently energised.

causes.label: Harness chafed through, short to ground
Shorted turns in the regulator coil (resistance too low)
Water or corrosion in the connector
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P0004.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit High
P0004.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. Open coil or wire, reported as high with ground-side switching
Connector fault at the regulator
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode
Rough running or diesel knock possible

P0005.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open
P0005.description: The fuel shutoff valve is a solenoid valve that opens or blocks the fuel supply. On diesel engines it is usually closed without current, so that the engine stops reliably when switched off. The engine control module energises it to let fuel flow and monitors its control circuit continuously. P0005 is set when this control circuit is open. A normally closed valve then cannot open, so the engine does not start or cuts out while driving. Which vehicles use this valve and code varies by manufacturer.

causes.label: Wire or connector interrupted or corroded
Valve coil open
Fuse or relay in the valve supply faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start

P0006.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Low
P0006.description: The fuel shutoff valve is a solenoid valve that opens or blocks the fuel supply. P0007.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High

P0008.title: Engine Position System Performance Bank 1
P0008.description: The engine control module learns how far each camshaft of bank 1 is offset from the crankshaft and compares this with a reference. P0008 is set when both camshafts of this bank are shifted in the same direction beyond a threshold. That points to the drive shared by the bank: a stretched primary timing chain, a worn tensioner, an idler gear or a crankshaft reluctor wheel that has slipped. A single faulty camshaft phaser does not set this code, because it affects only one camshaft.

causes.label: Primary or timing chain stretched
Chain tensioner worn or loose
Timing drive fitted incorrectly after an engine repair
Crankshaft reluctor wheel slipped

symptoms: Timing chain rattle, especially at cold start
Loss of power or rough running
Often stored together with P0016 to P0019

P000A.title: A Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 1
P000A.description: This monitor does not judge the end position of the intake camshaft on bank 1 but how fast it follows a change of the commanded angle. The code is set when the actual angle lags behind the target for too long during several adjustments. The adjustment speed depends directly on oil flow, so worn or wrong oil and a partly clogged screen are the usual causes. Drivability is often hardly affected; the fault is an early warning before the camshaft misses its target position altogether. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1.

Screen at the oil control valve partly clogged
Oil control valve sluggish
Cam phaser leaking internally or worn
Generally weak oil pressure, e.g. worn oil pump or bearings

P000E.title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Exceeded Learning Limit
P000E.description: The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. To compensate for tolerances and wear, the control module learns a long-term correction of the regulator control. P000E is set when this correction leaves its calibrated range. The regulator is electrically fine, but the system needs an unusually large correction all the time, which points to wear or contamination of regulator or pump, a weak low-pressure supply, or a missing calibration after a pump replacement.

causes.label: Fuel volume regulator worn or contaminated
High-pressure pump worn, delivering less
Low-pressure side: clogged filter, weak lift pump or air in the fuel
Not calibrated after pump or regulator replacement
Rail pressure sensor drifting

symptoms: Often hardly noticeable at first, later loss of power
Hard starting if rail pressure is wrong

P000F.title: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Activated
P000F.description: On common-rail diesel and some gasoline direct-injection systems a spring-loaded pressure relief valve protects the rail and injectors: if pressure rises too far, it opens and returns fuel to the tank, often holding a reduced pressure for limp-home operation. The control module recognises the opening from the rail pressure signal and stores P000F. The code reports an event, not a defect of the relief valve itself; the actual cause usually lies in pressure control, for example a regulator that delivers too much fuel.

causes.label: Fuel volume regulator stuck open or without current, pump over-delivers
Rail pressure sensor reading wrong, control runs into overpressure
Pressure control valve faulty, where fitted
Fuel return line blocked or kinked
Relief valve itself leaking or fatigued

symptoms: Sudden loss of power or limp mode

P0010.title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)
P0010.description: The engine control module drives the oil control valve (a pulse-width modulated solenoid) of the variable valve timing on the intake camshaft on bank 1. It checks the electrical state of this output and sets the code when the circuit is open, or when the measured state does not match the command, for example because of a short. Camshaft adjustment is then disabled and the phaser stays in its locked rest position: the engine keeps running, but with less torque and higher consumption. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1.

causes.label: Solenoid coil of the oil control valve open or shorted
Connector corroded, loose or soaked with engine oil wicking through the valve
Wiring harness chafed through or broken
Supply voltage missing, e.g. blown fuse
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less pulling power at low and medium engine speed

P0011.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1)
P0011.description: The engine control module compares the commanded position of the intake camshaft on bank 1 with the actual position it calculates from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. This code is set when the camshaft sits further advanced than commanded for longer than a calibrated time, or, depending on the manufacturer, when the target is missed in either direction ("system performance"). Typical cause is a phaser that does not return to its rest position, for example because the oil control valve sticks open or its screen is clogged. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1.

causes.label: Oil level too low, oil sludged or wrong viscosity
Screen at the oil control valve clogged with debris
Oil control valve mechanically sticking
Cam phaser worn or its locking pin sticking
Timing chain worn or fitted incorrectly after a repair

symptoms: Rough or unstable idle, as valve overlap is too large
Rattling from the timing drive at cold start

P0012.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)
P0012.description: The engine control module compares the commanded position of the intake camshaft on bank 1 with the actual position from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. This code is set when the camshaft stays further retarded than commanded for longer than a calibrated time. Usually the phaser does not move far enough out of its rest position, because oil pressure is too low to release the locking pin, the oil control valve does not open, or the oil screen is blocked. A stretched timing chain also shifts the camshaft towards retarded. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1.

causes.label: Oil pressure or oil level too low, oil worn out
Oil control valve sticking closed or its screen blocked
Cam phaser defective or seized in its rest position
Timing chain stretched or jumped a tooth
Wear debris in the oil circuit, e.g. from a thrust bearing

symptoms: Noticeably less torque and pulling power
Rattle from the timing drive if the chain is stretched

P0016.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
P0016.description: The engine control module checks whether the signal of the intake camshaft on bank 1 (sensor A) arrives at the expected crankshaft position, usually while the camshaft phaser is in its rest position. P0016 is set when the deviation stays outside a calibrated window. The camshaft is then out of step with the crankshaft: a timing belt or chain has jumped a tooth, the chain is stretched, the phaser is stuck at an end stop, or a reluctor wheel has slipped. On engines with a single camshaft, sensor A is simply the only camshaft sensor.

causes.label: Timing chain stretched, or belt or chain jumped a tooth
Camshaft phaser stuck at an end stop, oil control valve or oil pressure faulty
Incorrect assembly after a belt or chain replacement
Camshaft or crankshaft sensor signal disturbed
Reluctor wheel on crankshaft or camshaft slipped

symptoms: Rough idle and loss of power
Chain rattle at cold start on chain-driven engines
Risk of valve damage on interference engines if the timing has jumped

P001A.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P001A.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. Unlike a camshaft phaser it does not shift the timing continuously. The second letter "A" in the title numbers the actuator on this camshaft. This code is set when the control circuit of the actuator is open: no current flows when it is driven, because of a broken wire, an unplugged connector or an open coil. The engine usually stays on one profile, typically the base profile with low lift. Some manufacturers report these faults with their own codes instead.

causes.label: Connector at the actuator corroded, oil-soaked or loose
Wire broken, e.g. at the valve cover
Actuator coil open
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Less power at high engine speed because the profile does not switch
Higher consumption or uneven part-load running, depending on the profile

P0023.title: "B" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 2)

P002A.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P002A.description: A camshaft profile actuator switches the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. P0030.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0030.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) only delivers a usable signal once its ceramic element is hot. A heating element inside the sensor gets it there quickly after a cold start. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse or relay, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while comparing the commanded state with the measured voltage or current. Connector corroded or terminal pushed back
Heater supply fuse or relay faulty
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Closed-loop control starts late after a cold start
Emissions test or readiness check failed

P0033.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit

Output driver in the engine control module faulty

P0039.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Range/Performance

P003A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P003A.description: The electric boost actuator A positions the variable turbine vanes or the wastegate and reports its position through a sensor. P003C.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P003C.description: The camshaft profile actuator A switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 1 between fixed cam profiles, usually a low-lift base profile and a high-lift profile. In most designs the unactuated state ("off") is the base profile; which profile counts as "on" is defined by the manufacturer. The control module does not need a position sensor to check the switchover: it detects the actual profile indirectly, for example from oil pressure in the switching gallery, intake pressure per cylinder or crankshaft speed fluctuations. Oil supply to the switching elements leaking or restricted, e.g. worn seals
Locking pin in tappet or rocker arm, or sliding cam piece, sticking
Consequence of a circuit fault of the same actuator

symptoms: Lack of power at higher engine speed
Reduced power mode on some vehicles

P0040.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0040.description: On engines with two exhaust banks, the control module checks whether the upstream oxygen sensors are assigned to the right bank. It changes the mixture on one bank only, actively or as part of normal bank-wise control, and watches which sensor responds. If the sensor that should sit on the other bank reacts, the signals are swapped. This logic is documented for the manufacturer-specific predecessor codes; the usual cause is connectors plugged in crosswise after a repair. If the swap remains, each bank is controlled by the other bank's signal, so fuel trims drift towards their limits.

Harness routed wrongly or pins swapped in a connector
Wrong harness, control module or calibration after a replacement

symptoms: Fuel trim and mixture codes possible
Unstable idle or higher consumption possible

The system is rare and mainly found on older engines. P0065 means the control is electrically in order, but the effect is implausible. One documented method compares the idle speed controller correction with the air assistance switched on and off during stable idle; if the difference is too large, the code is set.

P0068.title: MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation
P0068.description: The engine control module compares the air quantity measured by the manifold pressure and/or mass air flow sensor with the quantity the throttle position leads it to expect. P0088.title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too High

P0095.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Bank 1

P009B.title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit/Open

For P00AE, the signal jumps faster than a real temperature can change, which typically points to a loose contact. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found. Bank 2 codes occur only on engines with two separate intake or charge-air paths, one per cylinder bank.

causes.label: Loose contact or wire broken by movement
Sensor failing intermittently
Interference on the signal wire

symptoms: Emissions test or readiness check may fail

P00AF.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Module Performance
P00AF.description: Boost control A here is an electronic actuator with its own electronics (a "smart" actuator), usually on the variable turbine geometry, with its own position sensor and controlled over a data bus or a pulsed signal. It checks itself and reports internal faults to the engine control module; documented examples are pattern errors, overcurrent and checksum errors. The control module cannot narrow down a fault inside the actuator further. P00AF is set when actuator A reports such an internal fault. Manufacturer bulletins recommend checking the vane mechanism for free movement and, if it moves freely, replacing only the actuator rather than the whole turbocharger.

causes.label: Electronics or motor inside the actuator faulty
Sector gear or vane mechanism sticking (soot, coking), causing overcurrent
Weak supply or ground, corroded connector
Software of actuator or control module

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode with reduced boost
Often stored with actuator position or boost codes

P00B0.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Module Performance
P00B0.description: Boost control B here is an electronic actuator with its own electronics (a "smart" actuator), usually on the variable turbine geometry, with its own position sensor and controlled over a data bus or a pulsed signal. It checks itself and reports internal faults to the engine control module; documented examples are pattern errors, overcurrent and checksum errors. The control module cannot narrow down a fault inside the actuator further. B denotes the second, separate actuator. P00B0 is set when actuator B reports an internal fault. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart.

causes.label: Electronics or motor inside the actuator faulty
Sector gear or vane mechanism sticking (soot, coking), causing overcurrent
Weak supply or ground, corroded connector
Software of actuator or control module

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode with reduced boost

P00B1.title: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit
P00B1.description: The radiator coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor that measures coolant temperature on the radiator side, typically at the radiator outlet; the exact position depends on the manufacturer. Together with the engine coolant temperature sensor it gives a second measuring point, which the control module uses to diagnose the thermostat and coolant flow, for example on engines with an electrically heated map-controlled thermostat. P00B1 is the general circuit fault; low and high signals have their own codes. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found.

causes.label: Connector or wiring at the radiator corroded or damaged (exposed front position)
Sensor faulty
Loose contact in the circuit
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Thermostat and coolant flow diagnostics are suspended

P00B2.title: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P00B2.description: The radiator coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor that measures coolant temperature on the radiator side, typically at the radiator outlet; the exact position depends on the manufacturer. Together with the engine coolant temperature sensor it gives a second measuring point, which the control module uses to diagnose the thermostat and coolant flow, for example on engines with an electrically heated map-controlled thermostat. P00B2 is a plausibility or range fault: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the operating state, for example because it is stuck at one value. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the exact logic is manufacturer-specific.

causes.label: Sensor drifting
Air at the sensor or low coolant level
Contact resistance at the connector
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Thermostat and coolant flow diagnostics are suspended

P00B3.title: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P00B3.description: The radiator coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor that measures coolant temperature on the radiator side, typically at the radiator outlet; the exact position depends on the manufacturer. Together with the engine coolant temperature sensor it gives a second measuring point, which the control module uses to diagnose the thermostat and coolant flow, for example on engines with an electrically heated map-controlled thermostat. P00B3 means the sensor resistance or signal voltage is very low, typically a short to ground; with an NTC sensor the control module then reads an extremely high temperature (around 150 °C in a documented case).

causes.label: Connector or wiring at the radiator corroded or damaged (exposed front position)
Sensor shorted internally
Signal wire shorted to ground
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Thermostat and coolant flow diagnostics are suspended

P00B4.title: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P00B4.description: The radiator coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor that measures coolant temperature on the radiator side, typically at the radiator outlet; the exact position depends on the manufacturer. Together with the engine coolant temperature sensor it gives a second measuring point, which the control module uses to diagnose the thermostat and coolant flow, for example on engines with an electrically heated map-controlled thermostat. P00B4 means the sensor resistance or signal voltage is very high, typically an open circuit or a short to the reference voltage; with an NTC sensor the control module then reads an extremely low temperature (around −60 °C in a documented case).

causes.label: Connector or wiring at the radiator corroded or damaged (exposed front position)
Sensor open internally
Signal wire broken or shorted to reference or battery voltage
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Thermostat and coolant flow diagnostics are suspended

P00B5.title: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P00B5.description: The radiator coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor that measures coolant temperature on the radiator side, typically at the radiator outlet; the exact position depends on the manufacturer. Together with the engine coolant temperature sensor it gives a second measuring point, which the control module uses to diagnose the thermostat and coolant flow, for example on engines with an electrically heated map-controlled thermostat. P00B5 is set when the signal jumps or drops out briefly, which typically points to a loose contact. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found.

causes.label: Connector or wiring at the radiator corroded or damaged (exposed front position)
Sensor faulty
Loose contact in the circuit
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Thermostat and coolant flow diagnostics are suspended

P00B6.title: Radiator Coolant Temperature/Engine Coolant Temperature Correlation
P00B6.description: The radiator coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor that measures coolant temperature on the radiator side, typically at the radiator outlet; the exact position depends on the manufacturer. Together with the engine coolant temperature sensor it gives a second measuring point, which the control module uses to diagnose the thermostat and coolant flow, for example on engines with an electrically heated map-controlled thermostat. After a long standstill (eight hours in a documented case) engine and radiator should be at the same temperature. P00B6 is set at the next start when the engine and radiator coolant temperature sensors differ by more than a threshold that may depend on intake air temperature. A detected engine block heater cancels the test. From this alone the control module cannot tell which sensor is wrong.

causes.label: Radiator coolant temperature sensor drifting
Engine coolant temperature sensor drifting
Contact resistance at a connector
Retrofitted engine preheater or auxiliary heater not detected by the system

P00B7.title: Engine Coolant Flow Low/Performance
P00B7.description: When the engine is hot, the thermostat should be open and coolant should flow through the radiator. P00B7 is set when the engine coolant temperature is very high (above about 117 to 119 °C in documented cases) while the radiator side stays much colder, so too little coolant flows through the radiator. The usual cause is a thermostat stuck closed; low coolant, air in the system, a pump that delivers too little or a blocked radiator have the same effect. If the temperature keeps rising, stop driving to avoid engine damage.

causes.label: Thermostat stuck closed
Low coolant level or air in the cooling system
Coolant pump delivering too little (impeller, drive; known cases on some engines)
Radiator or hoses blocked
One of the temperature sensors reading wrong

symptoms: High engine temperature up to overheating

P00B8.title: MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation Bank 2
P00B8.description: On engines with two intake paths, the control module compares the manifold pressure of bank 2 with the measured or calculated air quantity of that bank. P00B8 is set when the two do not fit together; the code does not say which value is wrong. As with its bank 1 counterpart, typical causes are an air leak, an exhaust gas recirculation valve that does not close, or a dirty or drifting sensor. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart.

causes.label: Air leak in the intake of bank 2
EGR valve dirty or sticking open
Manifold pressure sensor or air flow meter dirty or drifting
Wiring or connector faulty

P00B9.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low. Low Ambient Temperature
P00B9.description: This code reports too low a pressure in the low-pressure fuel supply between the lift pump and the high-pressure pump under the additional condition of low ambient temperature. It separates cold-related supply problems from the general case. A typical mechanism, documented for diesel engines, is wax separating from insufficiently winterised fuel at sub-zero temperatures and clogging the filter or tank strainer. No manufacturer description naming this exact code, its thresholds or the vehicles using it was found.

causes.label: Wax separation from summer or insufficiently winterised diesel in frost
Fuel filter clogged or water in the filter frozen
Fuel filter heater faulty
Lift pump weak

symptoms: Jerking or loss of power after starting

P00BA.title: Low Fuel Pressure - Forced Limited Power
P00BA.description: "Forced limited power" is a term for a protective strategy in which the engine control module deliberately limits engine power. Regulations require the check engine light to come on within seconds when such an emissions-relevant limp-home mode is active. These codes report the reason for the limitation; usually further codes point to the actual cause. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found. P00BA: power has been limited because fuel pressure is too low, which protects the engine and the pump against running lean or losing rail pressure.

causes.label: Fuel filter clogged, suction-side leak or air in the system
Lift pump or high-pressure pump weak
Pressure regulator or relief valve leaking
Tank run empty
Pressure sensor faulty

symptoms: Marked loss of power, limp mode

P00BB.title: Fuel Injector Insufficient Flow - Forced Limited Power
P00BB.description: "Forced limited power" is a term for a protective strategy in which the engine control module deliberately limits engine power. Regulations require the check engine light to come on within seconds when such an emissions-relevant limp-home mode is active. These codes report the reason for the limitation; usually further codes point to the actual cause. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found. P00BB: power has been limited because the injectors do not deliver enough fuel, for example due to coking or wear; low rail pressure or missing injector coding after a replacement have a similar effect.

causes.label: Injectors coked or worn (flow drift)
Fuel contamination
Rail pressure too low
Injector coding missing after replacement

symptoms: Marked loss of power, limp mode

P00BC.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow A Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too Low
P00BC.description: The control module compares the air mass measured by the air flow meter with the air mass it expects from a model, for example from manifold pressure, boost pressure and throttle position. These codes report the deviation with its direction: "too low" means the meter measures less air than expected, "too high" more. Regulations allow manufacturers to use one code for both directions or separate codes, as here. P00BC concerns air flow meter A. Typical causes are air entering behind the meter, a charge-air leak, a dirty meter or a restricted intake. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart.

causes.label: Air leak behind the meter or charge-air leak
Air flow meter dirty
Air filter or intake restricted
Wiring or connector faulty

P00BD.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow A Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too High
P00BD.description: The control module compares the air mass measured by the air flow meter with the air mass it expects from a model, for example from manifold pressure, boost pressure and throttle position. These codes report the deviation with its direction: "too low" means the meter measures less air than expected, "too high" more. Regulations allow manufacturers to use one code for both directions or separate codes, as here. P00BD concerns air flow meter A. Typical causes are a drifting or oil-coated meter or a wrong model value, for example from a faulty manifold pressure sensor or an open exhaust gas recirculation valve. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart.

causes.label: Air flow meter drifting or oil-coated
Model value wrong, e.g. faulty manifold pressure sensor or EGR valve stuck open
Leak upstream of the meter causing pulsations

P00BE.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow B Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too Low
P00BE.description: The control module compares the air mass measured by the air flow meter with the air mass it expects from a model, for example from manifold pressure, boost pressure and throttle position. These codes report the deviation with its direction: "too low" means the meter measures less air than expected, "too high" more. Regulations allow manufacturers to use one code for both directions or separate codes, as here. P00BE concerns air flow meter B, i.e. a second meter, for example in the second intake path of a V engine. Typical causes are air entering behind the meter, a charge-air leak, a dirty meter or a restricted intake. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart.

causes.label: Air leak behind the meter or charge-air leak
Air flow meter dirty
Air filter or intake restricted
Wiring or connector faulty

P00BF.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow B Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too High
P00BF.description: The control module compares the air mass measured by the air flow meter with the air mass it expects from a model, for example from manifold pressure, boost pressure and throttle position. These codes report the deviation with its direction: "too low" means the meter measures less air than expected, "too high" more. P00C0.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit
P00C0.description: Bypass valve B is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve of turbocharger B, not the wastegate: it lets charge air flow back to the compressor inlet when the throttle closes quickly, so the compressor does not surge. Turbocharger B is the second turbocharger in exhaust flow on series systems and the turbocharger of bank 2 on parallel twin-turbo engines. P00C0 is the general circuit fault, usually an open circuit in the control circuit of this valve; the circuit is monitored continuously.

causes.label: Wiring or connector damaged by turbocharger heat
Valve coil open or shorted
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Fluttering or surging noise when lifting off the throttle

P00C1.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit Low
P00C1.description: Bypass valve B is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve of turbocharger B, not the wastegate: it lets charge air flow back to the compressor inlet when the throttle closes quickly, so the compressor does not surge. Turbocharger B is the second turbocharger in exhaust flow on series systems and the turbocharger of bank 2 on parallel twin-turbo engines. P00C1 reports too low a voltage, typically a short to ground in the control circuit of this valve; the circuit is monitored continuously.

causes.label: Wiring or connector damaged by turbocharger heat

symptoms: Fluttering or surging noise when lifting off the throttle

P00C2.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit High
P00C2.description: Bypass valve B is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve of turbocharger B, not the wastegate: it lets charge air flow back to the compressor inlet when the throttle closes quickly, so the compressor does not surge. P00C3.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P00C3.description: Bypass valve B is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve of turbocharger B, not the wastegate: it lets charge air flow back to the compressor inlet when the throttle closes quickly, so the compressor does not surge. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart.

causes.label: Valve sticking or coked
Diaphragm or piston worn
Position feedback implausible

symptoms: Fluttering or surging noise when lifting off the throttle

P00C4.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B - Mechanical
P00C4.description: Bypass valve B is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve of turbocharger B, not the wastegate: it lets charge air flow back to the compressor inlet when the throttle closes quickly, so the compressor does not surge. Turbocharger B is the second turbocharger in exhaust flow on series systems and the turbocharger of bank 2 on parallel twin-turbo engines. P00C4 reports that the valve stays mechanically closed. A documented method detects this on overrun from the pulsation of the measured air mass that compressor surge causes when the valve should open.

causes.label: Valve stuck closed or coked
Diaphragm or piston worn
Valve not actuated correctly
Consequence of a boost or air flow fault

symptoms: Fluttering or surging noise when lifting off the throttle

P00C5.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Turbine Overspeed
P00C5.description: The control module has detected that turbocharger B runs above its permitted maximum speed. Speed is measured by a dedicated sensor per turbocharger where fitted, or estimated from a model of pressure ratio and air mass. Turbocharger B is the second turbocharger in series systems or the one on bank 2 in parallel systems. Typical causes are sticking boost control of this turbocharger or a charge-air leak; find the cause before driving on, as overspeed can destroy the turbocharger. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart.

causes.label: Boost control of turbocharger B sticking (wastegate or vanes)
Leak on the pressure side making the turbocharger work harder
Speed sensor or its wiring delivering wrong values
Operation at high altitude or software

P00C6.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
P00C6.description: Direct-injection engines release injection only once the rail has reached a minimum pressure. P00C6 is set when this pressure is not reached quickly enough while cranking, or, in another documented variant, when it drops below the minimum again right after the high-pressure start. Cranking then takes longer or the engine does not start. The check runs once per start; some manufacturers only enable it above a minimum tank level.

causes.label: High-pressure pump weak, or its drive cam or follower worn
Lift pump or low-pressure supply too weak
Control valve on the pump faulty
Leak or check valve fault letting pressure bleed off after shutdown
Very low fuel level

P00C7.title: Intake Air Pressure Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1
P00C7.description: With the engine stopped, all pressure sensors in the intake system (manifold pressure, boost pressure, barometric pressure) should read ambient pressure; some diesels also compare them at idle. The control module compares them: if one sensor stands out, it sets that sensor's own code. P00C7 is set when the readings disagree but no single sensor can be identified as faulty, which points to a fault affecting several sensors, such as a shared reference voltage or ground.

causes.label: Shared 5 V reference or ground of the pressure sensors disturbed
Two sensors drifting at the same time (contamination, oil mist, ageing)
Pressure hose to a sensor leaking or blocked
Engine control module or software

symptoms: Substitute values with loss of power possible

P00C8.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit/Open
P00C8.description: Some engine control modules switch the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator A on both sides: the ground side is monitored by P0090 to P0092, the supply side (high-side driver) by P00C8 to P00CA. On gasoline direct injection the regulator is typically the control valve on the high-pressure pump. P00C8 reports an open circuit on the supply side. Rail pressure can then not be controlled, causing starting problems, stalling or reduced power.

causes.label: Supply wire or connector to the pump solenoid damaged by heat or chafing
Solenoid coil open
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P00C9.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Low
P00C9.description: Some engine control modules switch the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator A on both sides: the ground side is monitored by P0090 to P0092, the supply side (high-side driver) by P00C8 to P00CA. On gasoline direct injection the regulator is typically the control valve on the high-pressure pump; on some diesels it is the regulator designated as regulator 1. P00C9 reports a short to ground on the supply side. Rail pressure can then not be controlled, causing starting problems, stalling or reduced power; documented systems turn on the warning light in the first drive cycle.

causes.label: Supply wire to the solenoid chafed and shorted to ground
Solenoid coil shorted
Water or corrosion in the connector
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P00CA.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit High
P00CA.description: Some engine control modules switch the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator A on both sides: the ground side is monitored by P0090 to P0092, the supply side (high-side driver) by P00C8 to P00CA. On gasoline direct injection the regulator is typically the control valve on the high-pressure pump; on some diesels it is the regulator designated as regulator 1. P00CA reports a short to battery voltage on the supply side, so the driver can no longer switch the supply off. Rail pressure can then not be controlled, causing starting problems, stalling or reduced power; documented systems turn on the warning light in the first drive cycle.

causes.label: Supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Water or corrosion in the connector
Internal fault in the solenoid
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P00CB.title: Fuel Volume Regulator Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit/Open
P00CB.description: The fuel volume regulator is the solenoid valve that meters how much fuel the high-pressure pump delivers (metering unit on diesels, pump control valve on some gasoline direct-injection engines). Many control modules switch such solenoids on both sides; P0001 to P0004 cover the control side, while these codes cover the supply side (high-side driver). P00CB reports an open circuit on the supply side. Rail pressure may then deviate, with reduced power or hard starting. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors.

causes.label: Supply wire broken or connector corroded
Regulator coil open or shorted (often built into the pump)
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P00CE.title: Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1
P00CE.description: After a long standstill (six hours in a documented case) all intake air temperature sensors, for example intake air, charge air cooler and manifold temperature, should read about the same. The control module compares them in pairs: if one sensor stands out, it sets that sensor's own plausibility code. This code is set when no pair agrees, so no single sensor can be identified as faulty. A detected engine preheater suspends the test. Since it runs only after a long standstill, the code may take a night to return after being cleared. Some vehicles also disable start-stop while this code is stored.

causes.label: One temperature sensor drifting without setting its own code
Uneven cooling, undetected preheater or strong sunshine
Shared ground or reference line disturbed, falsifying several sensors
Engine control module or software

P00CF.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation
P00CF.description: With the engine stopped or without boost, the boost pressure sensor A (between compressor and throttle) must read practically ambient pressure. This code is set when it deviates from the barometric pressure sensor by more than a threshold; the code does not say which of the two is wrong. Manufacturers that publish their diagnostics run the same comparison under other codes. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors.

causes.label: Boost pressure sensor dirty, oil-coated or drifting
Barometric sensor drifting, also when inside the control module
Contact resistance at connector, ground or 5 V reference
Sensor port or hose leaking or blocked

symptoms: Reduced boost or limp mode possible

P00D0.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Correlation
P00D0.description: With the engine stopped or without boost, the boost pressure sensor B (between compressor and throttle) must read practically ambient pressure. This code is set when it deviates from the barometric pressure sensor by more than a threshold; the code does not say which of the two is wrong. B denotes the second boost pressure sensor, for example on a second turbocharger. Manufacturers that publish their diagnostics run the same comparison under other codes. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors.

causes.label: Boost pressure sensor dirty, oil-coated or drifting
Barometric sensor drifting, also when inside the control module
Contact resistance at connector, ground or 5 V reference
Sensor port or hose leaking or blocked

symptoms: Reduced boost or limp mode possible

P00D1.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P00D1.description: This code concerns the heated oxygen sensor upstream of the catalytic converter (sensor 1) on bank 1. Unlike the heater circuit codes, which report an open or short circuit, this code means the heater is driven but does not bring the oxygen sensor to the expected temperature. One documented method, used where no current-measuring shunt is fitted, measures the internal impedance of the sensor element: a hot element has a low impedance. If the impedance stays above a limit that depends on the calculated element temperature and the voltage at the sensor connector, the heating is judged insufficient. The test runs once per trip. Typical causes are an aged heating element or added resistance from corrosion in the heater circuit. For this sensor position no manufacturer description of the test was found; the code appears in a manufacturer's code list, and the explanation follows the documented counterpart for sensor 2.

causes.label: Heating element aged, resistance increased
Corrosion or contact resistance at connector or harness of the heater circuit
Too low supply voltage at the sensor connector, e.g. poor ground
Diagnostic software (manufacturer updates exist for some vehicles)
Replacement sensor with a different heater

symptoms: Oxygen sensor heater readiness stays incomplete

P00F9.description: The turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A measures the pressure directly at the compressor outlet. It is a separate code family from the boost pressure sensor, which usually measures the pressure just ahead of the throttle; engines use it where the pressure behind the compressor is needed in addition, for example to judge the pressure loss across the charge air cooler or to protect against compressor surge. One manufacturer documents it as a combined temperature and pressure sensor. P00F9 means the signal is electrically valid but implausible. In a documented case the cause was a sensor not seated properly and a connector not fully engaged; securing them solved it without parts.

causes.label: Connector loose or not fully engaged, or sensor not seated properly
Sensor oil-coated from turbocharger oil mist or characteristic drifted
Leak at the sensor flange or seal
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode with boost limitation

P00FA.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P00FA.description: The turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A measures the pressure directly at the compressor outlet. It is a separate code family from the boost pressure sensor, which usually measures the pressure just ahead of the throttle; engines use it where the pressure behind the compressor is needed in addition, for example to judge the pressure loss across the charge air cooler or to protect against compressor surge. One manufacturer documents it as a combined temperature and pressure sensor. P00FA means the signal is below its valid range, typically an open circuit, a short to ground or a missing 5 V reference. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors.

causes.label: Connector loose or not fully engaged, or sensor not seated properly
Wire interrupted, short to ground or 5 V reference missing
Leak at the sensor flange or seal
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode with boost limitation

P00FB.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P00FB.description: The turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A measures the pressure directly after the compressor, usually ahead of the charge air cooler; FCA fits it as a combined temperature and pressure sensor. Boost control and compressor protection use the value. P00FB means the signal voltage is above its valid range: typically a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage, an open ground, or a failed sensor. It does not mean the boost really is too high – that would be P0234. The circuit is monitored continuously from key-on; comparable GM pressure sensors fail above 86–97 % of the reference for about 4 s. The engine then works with a substitute value and may limit boost. GM and Ford do not use this code family in their published summaries – they rely on the boost sensor ahead of the throttle (P0235–P0238) – so no manufacturer document naming exactly this code was found.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Ground (low reference) wire open or connector corroded
Sensor faulty internally (oil mist, heat at compressor outlet)
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode with boost limit

P00FC.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
P00FC.description: The turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A measures the pressure directly after the compressor, usually ahead of the charge air cooler; FCA fits it as a combined temperature and pressure sensor. Boost control and compressor protection use the value. P00FC covers short dropouts or jumps in the signal that are each too brief for the low or high code, or changes faster than real pressure can move. Comparable intermittent monitors count range violations per drive cycle – Ford's MAP check, for example, sets after 25 events. The FCA case for the sibling code P00F9 was a sensor not fully seated with an unlatched connector, exactly the kind of fault that produces erratic signals; heat and vibration near the turbocharger add to it. GM and Ford do not use this code family in their published summaries – they rely on the boost sensor ahead of the throttle (P0235–P0238) – so no manufacturer document naming exactly this code was found.

causes.label: Connector loose, not latched, or terminals corroded or spread
Harness chafed or broken near the turbocharger (heat, vibration)
Sensor with internal dropouts
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on, possibly only after several drives
Occasional hesitation or brief loss of power under load

P00FD.title: Battery B State of Charge Performance
P00FD.description: 'Battery B' here is not a hybrid high-voltage battery (those have codes from P0B27) but, in the only documented use by FCA/Stellantis, the 12 V auxiliary battery of the start-stop system. When the engine restarts automatically, a relay separates main and auxiliary battery so that the auxiliary one keeps the control units stable while the main battery cranks. The engine module sets P00FD if the auxiliary battery is disconnected on the first start, drops below about 8 V during an auto-start, or repeatedly falls below 10.3 V (counter reaches ten). Start-stop is then disabled; often it follows a jump start or many short trips. Whether the MIL comes on is not stated in the sources.

causes.label: Auxiliary battery discharged or aged
Loose or corroded positive or ground connections at either battery
150 A fuse or fuse array in the power distribution centre open or poorly contacting
Battery separation relay stuck
Main battery faulty

symptoms: Start-stop out of service, 'Service Start/Stop' message
'Service Shifter' message with electronic gear selector

P00FE.title: EVAP System Tank Vapor Line Restricted/Blocked
P00FE.description: The evaporative emission system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister and later purges it into the engine. P00FE means the vapour path between tank and canister is restricted or blocked. That matters because a blocked line can hide the tank side from the leak test and disturb tank venting and refuelling. Ford, where P00FE replaces its own code P144A, checks this once per drive cycle during the cruise leak test, while purging with the vent valve closed, and confirms suspicious pressure responses with an intrusive test. VW used the same code on the 2013–2019 Golf, where the diagnosis covers the purge valve and the leak detection module. Typical causes are kinked or pinched lines and charcoal grains from a broken canister.

causes.label: Kinked, pinched or misrouted vapour line between tank and canister
Charcoal canister broken down, grains blocking lines or valves
Rollover or fill-limit valve at the tank stuck closed (e.g. after overfilling)
Purge valve or leak detection module faulty
Tank pressure sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Fuel nozzle clicks off early when refuelling
Hiss or vacuum when opening the fuel cap

P00FF.title: Body Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P00FF.description: P00FF is an information code in the engine control module: the body control module has detected an emissions-relevant fault of its own and asks over the data bus for the check engine light. The engine module stores P00FF so that a generic OBD scanner can see why the MIL is on; the actual fault is stored in the body control module as B or U codes and must be read there. GM documents two cases – a 2020 Cadillac CT5 with climate flap actuator codes and 2025 full-size SUVs with U1962 – both cured by reprogramming the body control module, not by replacing parts. The mechanism matches other 'module requested MIL' codes such as P069E. P00FF itself causes no limp mode.

causes.label: Emissions-relevant fault in the body control module or its sensors/actuators (own B/U codes)
Software or calibration fault in the body control module
Communication fault on the data bus
Engine control module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on without an engine fault
Other messages depending on the body module fault
